ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to engagement, all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, senior managers, and material counterparties must be screened against: (i) OFAC SDN List and Consolidated Non-SDN List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU, UK, and PRC Ministry of Commerce consolidated sanctions lists; (iv) Hong Kong Monetary Authority and CEDB sanctions notices; and (v) PRC national blacklists, including Public Security Ministry wanted lists and SAMR prohibited registration lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, their family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth documentation to include audited accounts, bank references, and the contract chain. Screening must be repeated every 24 hours or upon adverse-media trigger, with audit trail retention for at least five years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation - National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), particularly Articles 23-34 on establishment, Articles 51-62 on corporate governance, Articles 91-101 on shareholder rights and registered capital; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019), Articles 6, 12, 30 and 31; Regulation on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (Order No. 746, State Council), Chapter II and Chapter IV
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Local Administration for Market Regulation at the municipal or district level where the WFOE is physically registered
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application, together with Notarized Articles of Association and the Name Approval Notice
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to this WFOE under PRC general law. The shareholders may set any registered capital amount in the Articles of Association. The entire subscribed capital must, however, be fully paid in within five (5) years from the date of the business license, unless the bank rules or sectoral regulations require earlier payment. There is no government escrow or blocked capital account requirement; contributions must be deposited into the company's bank basic account as ordinary paid-in capital and recorded in the statutory capital contribution register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD (the 'Company'), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company organized under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. This resolution is adopted as of the date of the execution of the incorporation documents at the Company's registered office. WHEREAS, the sole shareholder, a company incorporated in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, has subscribed for the entire initial share capital and requested the Board to complete the statutory incorporation and commence lawful business operations; WHEREAS, the Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC authorize the Board of Directors to manage the Company and to execute all matters necessary for establishment; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE. The Board ratifies the subscription of the registered capital of the Company, which shall be USD 50,000 or an equivalent amount in RMB, divided into 50,000 ordinary shares with a nominal value of USD 1.00 per share, all issued to the sole shareholder. The General Manager is authorized to open a dedicated capital contribution account, to collect the subscribed funds, to issue share certificates, and to prepare the capital contribution register as required by law. Any unpaid portion of the capital shall be contributed in full within five (5) years from the date of the business license, or earlier if the Articles of Association so stipulate. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATIONS. The Board designates the financial institutions named in the signed Appendix A as the Company's principal banks. Any two officers from the list comprised of the Executive Director, the General Manager and the Financial Controller shall jointly sign all bank account opening forms, deposit instruments, loan agreements and electronic payment instructions. The Board approves the affixing of the Company's legal seal and financial seal to all banking and treasury documents. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts as the Company's registered office the address set forth in the Articles of Association. The General Manager is authorized to execute and deliver an office lease agreement, to file the registered office with the competent Administration for Market Regulation, and to post the required statutory signage. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the persons named in Article 15 of the Articles of Association as Executive Director, Legal Representative, General Manager, Supervisor and Financial Responsible Person. Each officer shall exercise the powers and duties provided by law and by the Company's Articles of Association. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the Legal Representative and the General Manager, acting jointly or severally, to execute, file and deliver all applications, declarations, powers of attorney and other instruments necessary to obtain the business license, tax registration, social insurance registration, statistical registration and any industry permits required for the lawful operation of the Company. This Resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) online Enterprise Name Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the local AMR 'Enterprise Name Registration' portal and submit a proposed company name. The name must be structured as jurisdiction plus distinctive name plus industry plus 'Limited Liability Company' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered trade name or protected trademark. The applicant must also define the business scope using only lawful descriptions, namely the publishing and operation of lightweight ad-monetized mobile games and related software services. The authorized representative must upload scanned copies of the foreign investor's valid incorporation certificate and identity documents. The system issues a Name Approval Notice with a reservation period of six months. If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited elements, the applicant may amend the name and resubmit within three business days without losing queue priority.
required_dossiers: Passport or business identity document of the ultimate beneficial owner
Notarized certificate of incorporation of the Hong Kong parent company
Proposed company name in English and Chinese transliteration
Draft business scope description
Board or shareholder resolution authorizing the incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is queried or suspended due to prior trademark conflict or ambiguous industry description, file a formal re-examination application with the local AMR or adopt an alternate name approved in advance. The suspension is curable within three business days by submitting the corrective naming statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Establishment Registration and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) registration window or Government Integrated Service Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete establishment application package to the AMR office or through the online integrated platform. The package must include the signed Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application, the fully executed Articles of Association, evidence of the registered office lease, the landlord's property ownership certificate or consent letter, valid identification documents for the legal representative, supervisor and general manager, the Name Approval Notice, and the foreign investor's notarized and legalized incorporation documents. The AMR will examine the legality of the governance structure, the capital contribution rules and the business scope. Upon approval, the AMR issues the Business License with a unified social credit code. All supporting documents must be in Chinese or accompanied by certified translations, and the legal representative must be present for identity verification if required by local practice.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application form
Notarized Articles of Association
Office lease agreement and real estate ownership certificate
Identification documents of legal representative, supervisor and general manager
Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation of the Hong Kong shareholder
Name Approval Notice
Commitment letter on truthful registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a correction notice, the applicant has fifteen working days to cure any insufficiency in the documents or governance provisions. If the application is formally rejected, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days or bring an administrative lawsuit within six months before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Registrations (Tax, Social Insurance and Statistics)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and local Statistical Authority via the integrated one-stop service portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after issuance of the Business License, the Company must complete all post-registration formalities through the integrated multi-license consolidation process. The Company must obtain a taxpayer identification number and tax registration certificate, register with social insurance schemes and open a social insurance contribution account, and file statistical registration data with the local authority. The financial responsible person must submit the business license, legal representative identification, bank account information and company seal specimen. The authorities will verify the business scope and the employer registration. Any change in the legal representative or registered address must be updated contemporaneously. The one-stop portal issues an electronic registration receipt confirming completion.
required_dossiers: Business License with unified social credit code
Legal representative identification document
Articles of Association and incorporation resolution
Basic bank account opening certificate
Company seals and specimen imprints
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any required document is missing or rejected, the applicant can upload a supplementary explanation through the same portal. Overdue registrations may attract late filing fines; the Company may apply for retroactive compliance if the delay was caused by force majeure, supported by a sworn statement and the original evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the PRC, with foreign exchange registration through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) if the capital is contributed in foreign currency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a licensed commercial bank and execute the account opening application together with the Banking Authorization Resolution adopted by the Board. The bank will verify the identity of the signatories, collect the corporate seal and financial seal impressions, and open the basic deposit account. Once the account is active, the sole shareholder must transfer the subscribed capital into the account. For foreign currency contributions, the bank and the Company must complete the SAFE foreign exchange registration on the Capital Project Foreign Exchange Information System and provide a source-of-funds declaration. If the Articles require a capital verification report, a PRC-registered accountant must issue the report and deliver it to the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Business License
Articles of Association
First Board Resolution including banking authorization
Company legal seal and financial seal
Legal representative passport or ID card
Source of funds declaration for foreign exchange contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account opening due to AML/KYC doubts, the Company must supply audited financial statements of the shareholder or a certified bank reference. If SAFE requests corrections, refile the foreign exchange declaration within ten working days to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Statutory Books and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registered office and corporate governance records, with optional file copies at the local AMR and tax bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license and bank account are in place, the Company secretary or governance officer must assemble the statutory books at the registered office. The records shall include the share capital register, minutes of the sole shareholder, the First Board Resolution, appointment letters for each officer, seal custody logs, and copies of all governmental filings. These records must be kept in chronological order and made available for inspection by shareholders, tax authorities and the market regulator. If the registered address later changes, the Company must file a notice with the AMR and update the bank and tax files within thirty days.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution
Share capital register
Officer appointment letters and acceptances
Registered office lease and property certificate
Seal imprint specimen and custody register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory record is incomplete or lost, the Board must adopt a corrective resolution and file a supplementary declaration with the AMR and the tax authorities. In cases of unauthorized seal use, the Company must file a police report and issue a lost-seal notice before replacing the seal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital software publisher, no industrial plant, factory or physical production facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 5820 software publishing does not require an operating license from an industrial licensing board.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment is required for a pure digital software publishing company that generates no industrial discharges, air emissions or hazardous waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero manufacturing or chemical processing output. The registered office must, however, comply with general municipal wastewater discharge standards (COD below 500 mg/L, pH between 6 and 9) and ordinary solid waste collection rules, but no industrial discharge permit or EIA is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to industrial licensing. The leased office premises must nevertheless obtain a standard Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (消防安全检查合格证) if the space is classified as a public gathering place under the PRC Fire Services Law. For a non-public office area, the Company must perform a self-assessment and keep fire extinguishers, emergency lighting and exit signage in compliance with the local fire code. Occupational safety requirements under the PRC Occupational Disease Prevention and Work Safety Laws apply to office ergonomics, electrical safety and data server rooms, but no civil defense clearance is required for a purely digital operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), acting through provincial, municipal and district tax service bureaus; the national online service portal is the Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax Bureau) of the State Taxation Administration, accessible on the official STA web platform (www.chinatax.gov.cn).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the PRC-established Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the statutory Tax Identification Number is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) shown on the business license issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); tax registration is completed automatically through the multi-license joint registration data-sharing mechanism, followed by online tax-type confirmation, legal representative and finance-officer filing, bank account reporting, and accounting-standard declaration via the E-Tax Bureau within 30 days of establishment. The WFOE must then determine its VAT taxpayer identity: small-scale taxpayer (annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000) or general VAT taxpayer (mandatory above that threshold or voluntary election). For the Hong Kong non-resident parent, no PRC TIN is required unless it directly derives PRC-sourced income through a taxable presence; if dividend or other China-source payments are made to the Hong Kong parent, the Hong Kong tax residence certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department of the Hong Kong SAR (along with beneficial-owner declaration) is used to support reduced treaty withholding under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement. If a foreign non-resident enterprise is itself required to register for PRC tax purposes, it must register with the STA through the E-Tax Bureau as a non-resident enterprise taxpayer and obtain a PRC taxpayer identification number before filing and paying China-source income tax and VAT withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the PRC does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election. The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income. VAT elections are limited to the small-scale taxpayer versus general VAT taxpayer status election; cross-border service supplies may be claimed as zero-rated or exempt in accordance with VAT pilot rules, but this is a claim-based determination rather than a corporate tax election. Hybrid mismatch and anti-deferral adjustments apply under the special tax adjustment measures of China's Corporate Income Tax Law; no elective entity classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the VAT pilot framework of the People's Republic of China (Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration joint rules replacing business tax with VAT); no provincial sales tax or separate GST applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable sales) is the mandatory threshold for general VAT taxpayer status; below this threshold a Chinese small-scale taxpayer rate applies, although voluntary general taxpayer registration is available. A foreign company with no PRC establishment does not have a registration threshold for supplies consumed in China; instead, the PRC buyer or payer withholds VAT at source unless the overseas supplier voluntarily registers for cross-border e-commerce VAT settlement under STA practice.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-invoicing taxpayers must use the national E-Tax Bureau electronic invoicing system with a tax UKey or the fully digitalized electronic invoice (all-digital electronic invoice) module; each invoice is generated with a unique invoice code and number and digitally signed before transmission to the State Taxation Administration's national VAT invoice system. General VAT taxpayers must maintain a tax-control device, issue VAT special or general invoices in real time, and submit invoice data during the prescribed filing cycles; the authority conducts automated real-time data matching and anti-fraud digital stamping of invoice information. API-based e-invoicing is available for enterprises with high-volume invoicing through approved electronic invoice service platforms integrated with the STA, while all-digital electronic invoices eliminate the physical invoicing seal requirement and are cleared in the STA's invoice database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on exported goods applies when the goods are declared to customs, physically leave the customs territory of China, and export proceeds are repatriated to a PRC bank account in accordance with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange rules. 0% VAT export treatment for qualifying cross-border services applies to services provided to an overseas entity and fully consumed outside China, including software and information-technology services, advertising services, and related digital services supplied by the WFOE to overseas ad networks such as AdMob and AppLovin, under the cross-border taxable services zero-rating and exemption provisions of the VAT pilot framework (including the cross-border services catalogue and the STA management measures for zero-rated services tax refunds or exemptions). The business must prove the foreign residence of the service recipient, the delivery and performance of the service outside China, and the receipt of payment in foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Goods export: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration filed through the China International Trade Single Window), original or electronic Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, commercial invoice, packing list, and the export contract.

Goods export foreign-exchange record: Bank inward remittance certificate or bank foreign-exchange settlement and repatriation record (equivalent to Inward Remittance Certificate, FIRC) evidencing receipt and settlement of export proceeds within the statutory deadline.

Cross-border services zero-rating file: Cross-border service agreement with the non-resident ad network, PRC VAT special or general invoice or zero-rated export invoice, bank remittance certificate for the service fees, certificate of Hong Kong or other non-resident tax status of the service recipient, and service-performance logs (user geolocation, ad-serving reports) proving the advertising services were consumed outside the Chinese customs and tax territory.

Export refund or exemption application package: Software copyright registration file where required, software product assessment report where an exported software product refund is claimed, and the export tax refund or zero-rating credit declaration submitted through the E-Tax Bureau.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misapplied export zero-rating, false customs declarations, forged Bills of Lading, or fabricated foreign-exchange remittance records expose the WFOE to retrospective clawback of the previously zero-rated or refunded VAT, recovery of underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest at 0.05%, and administrative penalties of 50% to 5 times the tax evaded under the Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Where the conduct is classified as fraudulent export tax refund, the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China applies, and convictions may result in confiscation of proceeds, fines, confiscation of property, and criminal imprisonment for the responsible persons. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange may additionally impose penalties for non-repatriation of export proceeds or false foreign-exchange documentation, and the tax authority may disqualify the taxpayer from future export VAT refund eligibility and audit the prior three to five years' filings, with no time limitation in cases of fraudulent concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) regulates the offshore CNH clearing node
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed, partially convertible foreign exchange framework. Current-account revenue, including export sales, software royalties, and ad-network settlements, is generally convertible after a licensed bank performs a genuine transaction review. Capital-account flows are not freely convertible: inbound equity, shareholder loans, guarantees, and outward remittances require State Administration of Foreign Exchange registration or approval, dedicated capital accounts, and post-transaction reporting. The renminbi is deliverable onshore at the CNY rate and offshore in Hong Kong at the CNH rate; a WFOE must keep its operating foreign currency receipts onshore and route settlement through a licensed PRC bank. Profit remittance to the Hong Kong parent is lawful only when supported by audited financial statements, a board resolution, income tax settlement certificates, and SAFE-monitored bank documents. Material deviation between declared ad revenue and bank deposits triggers regulatory review. The entity therefore has no free convertibility for speculative capital movements, and current-account convertibility remains conditional on document authenticity. The Hong Kong side is not subject to China's FX controls, but is only an offshore clearing node, not a substitute for onshore SAFE compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The old compulsory surrender ratio has been abolished. A compliant WFOE may retain 100 percent of export and service-trade foreign currency in a domestic FX settlement account or voluntarily convert it to RMB. However, the proceeds must be repatriated to a qualified domestic bank account by the contractually agreed payment date and reported in the SAFE trade monitoring system. For goods trade, unreceived export proceeds beyond 90 days after the declared export date require special anomaly reporting unless a valid extension has been registered; for service trade, ad-network payouts follow the platform payment schedule, but overdue receipts beyond 180 days must be explained with contract and reconciliation evidence. Banks apply a real-need verification to every settlement, requiring contracts, invoices, and a transaction code declaration. The mandatory sale ratio is nil; conversion is at enterprise discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account, RMB Capital Settlement Account, and Basic Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Deposit Account, Foreign Exchange Settlement Account, and Cross-Border Payment Warehousing
Operational Currency Account and RMB Clearing through CIPS for Hong Kong-related flows
Secondary FX Settlement Account for ad-network payouts and foreign-currency vendor payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW and legally inappropriate for the onshore WFOE. Offshore digital EMIs are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE and cannot operate a RMB deposit account, FX settlement, or FDI capital account for a Mainland China entity. Their cross-border collection tools would expose the WFOE to illegal third-party settlement charges and undermine bank trust. The Hong Kong parent may use reputable EMIs as an ancillary collection layer for USD/HKD ad-platform payouts only before netting the treasury into the onshore WFOE; this does not satisfy PRC treasury or SAFE requirements. All onshore liquidity must be cleared through a Tier-1 domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PRC Tier-1 banks require the legal representative or a highly authorized officer to attend a live KYC interview at a physical branch; remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted. Most banks perform a two-person field verification at the WFOE registered office and require the company seal, articles of association, business license, original passports or identity cards, and proof of registered address. If the legal representative is based in Hong Kong, a physical visit to the mainland branch is the safest route; BOC cross-border relationship coordination may reduce friction, but the onshore statutory identity must still be satisfied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly incorporated WFOE in lightweight mobile game publishing is expected to receive large monthly ad-network payouts from offshore platforms before demonstrating physical office or employee substance, creating a phantom-trade or money-mule suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease contract for the WFOE registered address, payroll and social insurance records, publisher contracts with AdMob and AppLovin, platform payout statements, SDK/API traffic analytics, monthly revenue reconciliation with bank FX deposits, and audited prior-month financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ownership chain crosses a Hong Kong holding company into the Chinese WFOE, and the bank may suspect disguised nominee shareholders or undisclosed mainland controllers for tax evasion or sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Hong Kong Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, significant-controller register, full ownership chain for HK parent and WFOE, passports of ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-funds documents for the equity injection, and a corporate wealth statement showing operating substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad revenue enters and is immediately converted into RMB and disbursed to payroll, rent, and third-party vendors, producing a layering pattern typical of informal money transfer systems.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticity declarations for each received stream, foundation service contracts, invoice and official tax invoice documentation, supplier agreements, payroll tax returns, social insurance filings, rental receipts, and a treasury policy that prevents same-day conversion and disbursement without matching transaction tags.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outward remittances to the Hong Kong parent for intellectual property license fees or group support are similar to disguised dividend distribution and capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technology license agreement registered with the local technology import authority, MOFCOM and SAFE registration records, transfer-pricing study and contemporaneous documentation, service records and time sheets, tax withholding certificates for remittance, and audited financial statements of both entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The HK parent must remit equity funds via SWIFT MT103 to the BOC or ICBC FDI capital account using an inward direct investment purpose code and the WFOE SAFE registration reference as beneficiary identifier. Upon credit, the WFOE submits a capital account settlement application to the bank, converts the funds into RMB under the approved negative-list use conditions, and instructs a licensed PRC accounting firm to issue a capital verification report. The verified paid-in capital is then reported to SAFE and the business registration system. The funds may only be used for wages, rents, domestic procurement and taxes, and prohibited uses include on-lending, entrusted loans, and speculative investments without further SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the principal rail for high-value operational remittances, tax payments, and related-party royalties. Commercial letters of credit are suitable for significant procurement or software licensing when a bank undertaking is required, while documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are reserved for trusted trade partners where cash settlement risk is moderate. Each outbound payment requires the original invoice, service contract, proof of service acceptance, corporate income tax withholding certificate, and SAFE transaction declaration. RMB-denominated cross-border payments to the Hong Kong parent should be routed through CIPS with the CNH account details and underlying contract reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts under the real-need principle for ad-revenue conversion and operating FX exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for non-speculative hedging of foreign-currency intercompany debt or external loans
FX swaps for short-term swapping of CNY and foreign-currency liquidity with the same domestic bank
Licensed PRC bank exchange-rate options (call or put) with documented genuine commercial underlying
Offshore non-deliverable forwards are impermissible for the onshore WFOE and may only be executed by the Hong Kong treasury vehicle outside mainland China to hedge CNH volatility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation, without reliance on any Gazette extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate by period: over 42 days to 3 months, HKD 1,200 (USD 154); over 3 to 6 months, HKD 2,400 (USD 308); over 6 to 9 months, HKD 3,600 (USD 462); over 9 months, HKD 4,800 (USD 615). Repeated default exposes the company to prosecution under section 662(7) of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and administrative strike-off under section 744, with gazetted notice and eventual dissolution unless the company resumes active filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the current certificate expiry date; the renewal notice issued one month before expiry prescribes the final payment due date and any grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts the statutory late fee (currently HKD 300, approximately USD 38) and causes the prior certificate to lapse. Carrying on business without an effective Business Registration Certificate is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), punishable by a fine of up to HKD 5,000 and imprisonment for up to 6 months. Continued non-renewal may block tax clearance and, together with non-filing of returns, support strike-off action under the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued on a staggered basis; ordinarily due within 1 month from the issue date. A qualified Hong Kong tax representative may obtain automatic filing extensions to 15 August for a 31 December year end and to 15 November for a 31 March year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under section 80(2) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, exposing the company to a fine of HKD 10,000 (approximately USD 1,282). The Inland Revenue Department may also issue a best-of-assessment and impose additional tax of up to 10% of the tax undercharged. This does not directly trigger administrative strike-off, but unresolved tax liabilities and uncoordinated filings impair tax clearance and can indirectly support compulsory winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and IR56B employee statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Employment Tax Unit, Hong Kong
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued annually on or about 1 April; due within one month of the issue date, generally by 30 April. Changes of employees or cessation of employment also require filing within 1 month of the relevant event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under section 80(1) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, carrying a fine of up to HKD 10,000 (approximately USD 1,282) per irregularity. Wilful understatement or deliberate omission of employee remuneration may result in additional tax assessments of up to three times the amount undercharged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements with Auditor's Report and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (submitted with the Profits Tax Return) and members/shareholders of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company, the directors must send the financial statements and auditor's report to members within 9 months after the end of the financial year; for the first accounting period, within 18 months after incorporation. Audited accounts accompany the BIR51 filing by the IRD-stipulated due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare, sign and deliver financial statements in accordance with sections 429 and 431 of the Companies Ordinance are liable to prosecution and fines up to HKD 300,000 (approximately USD 38,462) plus a daily default fine of up to HKD 7,500 (approximately USD 962). For profits tax purposes, failure to submit audited financial statements attracts the same sanctions as an unsatisfied Profits Tax Return, including best-of-assessment and additional tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Significant Controllers Register (SCR) Review and Confirmation Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office or prescribed place in Hong Kong, maintained for inspection by law enforcement and authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual filing to the Companies Registry is required; the register must be updated within 7 days of any change in significant control, and an internal annual confirmation should be completed no later than the NAR1 due date, i.e. 42 days after the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the Significant Controllers Register under Schedule 5A of the Companies Ordinance is an offence, with a fine of up to HKD 25,000 (approximately USD 3,205) and a continuing default fine of up to HKD 700 per day. Each material omission or false entry is a separate offence, and the designated representative may be personally liable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There are no quantitative turnover, total-asset or employee thresholds that waive audit for a non-dormant Hong Kong company. Every company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) must appoint a certified public accountant as auditor and have its financial statements audited, unless it is dormant and validly claims exemption under section 373. A private company may qualify as a small private company under section 359D if it satisfies at least two of three tests: annual revenue not exceeding HKD 100 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 100 million, and employees not exceeding 100. That status permits simplified financial reporting under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance but does not eliminate the statutory audit obligation. Dormant exemption is available only when the company has passed a dormant resolution, filed the prescribed declaration with the Companies Registry, and has not entered into any pecuniary transaction during the exemption period.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are aligned with IFRS, issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants. Eligible private entities may apply the HKFRS for Private Entities framework. Small private companies may prepare simplified financial statements under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance. Audits must be conducted in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing by an auditor licensed under the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council ordinance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Schedule 5A of the Companies Ordinance, a Hong Kong company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at its registered office or a prescribed location and record any relevant change in significant control within 7 days of becoming aware of it. There is no standalone annual UBO filing with the Companies Registry; however, an internal annual confirmation should be performed before the Annual Return due date, and the designated representative must, on request, make the SCR available to law enforcement and relevant authorities within 24 hours. For the Chinese cross-border ownership limb, any direct equity transfer in the PRC WFOE or charge over such equity is reportable to the State Administration for Market Regulation and the foreign investment information reporting system within 30 days of the change, and the Hong Kong register of members and SCR should be updated in parallel to maintain a consistent group ownership record. All shareholding transfer instruments, SCR updates, board resolutions and related confirmations should be retained for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretary

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 385 - 1,923 per annum (equivalent to HKD 3,000 - 15,000) for registered office address, company secretary services, statutory mailbox and basic compliance administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 5,000 per annum for a low-risk hyper-casual mobile gaming company with typical transaction volume, assuming HKFRS audit, tax computation and standard corporate secretarial coordination

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard PRC Corporate Income Tax rate under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 4
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for High-and-New-Technology Enterprise (HNTE) qualification; 10% national key software enterprise rate for qualifying software publishers; 100% super deduction for qualified R&D expenses; location-based preferential free-zone incentives apply only if the WFOE is registered in a designated encouraged industry zone such as Hainan Free Trade Port or Qianhai, and none apply automatically to a standard Shanghai/Shenzhen WFOE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (General Regime A class) and quarterly prepayment return Form A200000, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic tax office and local provincial e-Tax portals
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional prepayment returns
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment return due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; annual final filing due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e. for a calendar-year WFOE the annual filing and settlement deadline is May 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from hyper-casual game publishing and monetization, including all AdMob and AppLovin payout proceeds, in-app purchases, and advertising revenue; platform fees must not be netted against revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PRC WFOE is a China tax resident and must declare worldwide income; convert foreign-currency ad revenue using the monthly average or spot exchange rate announced by the State Taxation Administration and keep platform payout statements, bank slips, and revenue-sharing contracts as evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report direct costs of game development, app store commissions, server hosting, content licensing, outsourced production, and direct cost of game publishing services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the Hong Kong shareholder or offshore service providers are deductible only if supported by contracts, invoicing, actual benefit received, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; intra-group service charges without demonstrable benefit are non-deductible under EIT Law Article 40

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax, land use tax, and other taxes that are deductible as expenses for CIT purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is not itself deducted in the income tax return; import VAT on cross-border services and royalties is outside the CIT cost base and must be handled through the VAT system separately

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report user acquisition costs, CPI/CPM advertising, creative production, app store optimization, social media marketing, and royalties paid for licensed gaming content
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advertising and marketing services purchased from the Hong Kong related party must satisfy the arm's length standard and the benefit test; if the local file threshold is triggered, a benchmarking study must be contemporaneously prepared to avoid transfer pricing adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report salaries, rent, depreciation, management fees, legal and accounting fees, and general overhead expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharges or management fees paid to the Hong Kong parent or group head office are generally not deductible if they are passive allocations rather than specific services; a service agreement, evidence of actual performance, and cost allocation methodology must be retained

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest on shareholder loans, bank borrowings, foreign exchange losses, and related financing charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the Hong Kong shareholder is subject to PRC withholding tax at 10% unless the 7% Hong Kong DTA rate applies; the WFOE must also respect thin capitalization limits of 2:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial enterprises, and interest deductibility requires TRC and beneficial ownership documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Additions and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax-exempt income, reduced income, and special additional deductions, especially the 100% R&D super deduction for qualifying game engine and software research activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D expenses outsourced to overseas related parties are included in the super deduction only under the statutory limitations; document the R&D project plan, personnel time records, and cost breakdown to withstand scrutiny from the tax authority

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8 - Taxable income after reconciliation adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable income through the A105000 adjustment schedule, including transfer pricing adjustments, disallowed related-party charges, thin cap interest, and tax loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 5-year loss carryforward applies to normal losses; transfer pricing adjustments will increase taxable income, and any loss brought forward from prior years must be supported by the annual loss declaration and tax filings

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory or preferential rate to taxable income, then offset quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits to compute final tax due or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend withholding tax is not computed in this box because it is triggered at the time of profit distribution; use the separate withholding declaration system and do not confuse the WFOE's own CIT liability with the non-resident shareholder's WHT liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual or quarterly CIT return triggers a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 62; late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% under Article 32; underpayment caused by false or fraudulent declaration attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid under Article 63; criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 applies when the concealed tax exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax due, with imprisonment up to 7 years possible, and the entity can be blacklisted as a serious tax violation by the State Taxation Administration
